1 · Intro

When to use it.

Most student and faculty transactions in Oracle go to approval before they take effect. Knowing the basics helps you track them and fix stuck ones before payroll cutoff.

Vanderbilt's approval routing for these populations is still being confirmed.

Use this whenYou submitted a student or faculty transaction and need to know where it is and who must act.

2 · Walk through

What to know.

Check off each item as you read.

Watch-outs

  • A transaction that is not approved does not take effect. Check the bell before payroll cutoff.
  • Open item: Vanderbilt approval routing for student, faculty, emeritus, FERDC, stipend, and expense-only transactions (who approves each) is not yet documented.
  • Open item: Who at Vanderbilt can use Transaction Console or Quick Convert, which skips approval.

Official documentation

Vendor documentation describes the standard process. Vanderbilt's setup, codes, and rules in this course take priority.

  • Oracle: How You Manage HCM Approval Transactions (opens in a new tab)

HCM Academy job aid · Changes and Approvals

Oracle transactions and approvals for these populations

Use when: You submitted a student or faculty transaction and need to know where it is and who must act. · System: Oracle HCM

  1. Know which transactions need approval.
  2. Track your transactions with the notifications bell at the top of Oracle.
  3. Know Oracle's default rules.
    • Submitter cannot self-approve
    • Withdraw is allowed by default
  4. If a transaction is stuck, contact the right person before cutoff.

Watch-outs

  • A transaction that is not approved does not take effect. Check the bell before payroll cutoff.
  • Open item: Vanderbilt approval routing for student, faculty, emeritus, FERDC, stipend, and expense-only transactions (who approves each) is not yet documented.
  • Open item: Who at Vanderbilt can use Transaction Console or Quick Convert, which skips approval.
